sec-eval-4.title: Dangerous Code Execution via eval()
sec-eval-4.message: Use of eval() detected. Arbitrary code execution vulnerability.
sec-eval-4.explanation: eval() passes a string directly into the JavaScript interpreter. If user input flows into eval(), attackers can execute arbitrary code.
sec-eval-4.risk: Remote Code Execution (RCE) and full application compromise.
sec-eval-4.suggestion: Refactor to parse JSON using JSON.parse() or use safe data mappings instead of dynamic code execution.

sec-sqli-3.title: SQL Injection via String Concatenation
sec-sqli-3.message: SQL statement constructed via string concatenation or interpolated template literals.
sec-sqli-3.explanation: Concatenating untrusted dynamic variables into SQL query strings enables SQL injection.
sec-sqli-3.risk: Direct database exfiltration, unauthorized administrative access, or database deletion.
sec-sqli-3.suggestion: Use parameterized queries with placeholders ($1, ?, or named parameters) and pass arguments separately.

sec-crypto-16.title: Weak Cryptographic Hash Algorithm (MD5)
sec-crypto-16.message: Use of broken cryptographic hash algorithm: md5.
sec-crypto-16.explanation: MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks and should never be used for password hashing, digital signatures, or security tokens.
sec-crypto-16.risk: Hash collision attacks and security token forgery.
sec-crypto-16.suggestion: Use SHA-256 / SHA-512 for integrity, or bcrypt / argon2 / scrypt for password hashing.

bug-assign-in-cond-19.title: Accidental Assignment in Conditional Statement
bug-assign-in-cond-19.message: Assignment operator (=) found inside conditional statement where comparison (===) was likely intended.
bug-assign-in-cond-19.explanation: This assigns a value rather than comparing it, resulting in the condition always evaluating to truthy/falsy based on the assigned value.
bug-assign-in-cond-19.risk: Logic errors, accidental infinite loops, or bypassed security checks.
bug-assign-in-cond-19.suggestion: Replace "=" with "===" for strict equality comparison.

quality-debugger-24.title: Debugger Statement in Code
quality-debugger-24.explanation: Debugger statements halt execution when developer tools are open and must never be committed to production code.
quality-debugger-24.risk: Application freezing in client browsers and accidental exposure of runtime state.
quality-debugger-24.suggestion: Remove debugger statement before committing or deploying.

sec-xss-32.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via innerHTML
sec-xss-32.message: Direct assignment to innerHTML risks DOM Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
sec-xss-32.explanation: Setting innerHTML directly with dynamic content allows malicious scripts to execute within the victim browser session.
sec-xss-32.risk: Session hijacking, credential theft, and unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.
sec-xss-32.suggestion: Use element.textContent, innerText, or sanitize HTML using DOMPurify before inserting.

sec-hardcoded-secret-6.title: Hardcoded Secret or API Key Detected
sec-hardcoded-secret-6.message: Hardcoded secret, API key, or credential found in source code.
sec-hardcoded-secret-6.explanation: Committing hardcoded secrets into version control exposes credentials to anyone with repository read access or data leaks.
sec-hardcoded-secret-6.risk: Credential leak, unauthorized API access, and infrastructure compromise.
sec-hardcoded-secret-6.suggestion: Store secrets in environment variables (.env) and access via process.env.

sec-sqli-12.title: SQL Injection via String Concatenation
sec-sqli-12.message: SQL statement constructed via string concatenation or interpolated template literals.
sec-sqli-12.explanation: Concatenating untrusted dynamic variables into SQL query strings enables SQL injection.
sec-sqli-12.risk: Direct database exfiltration, unauthorized administrative access, or database deletion.
sec-sqli-12.suggestion: Use parameterized queries with placeholders ($1, ?, or named parameters) and pass arguments separately.
